study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative modeling analysis reveals corpus callosum volume changes in early and mid-to-late first episode major depression

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: This study investigated corpus callosum (sub)volume differences between first-episode major depressive disorder (MDD) patients and healthy controls using normative modeling. It also examined how early versus mid-to-late onset first depressive episodes and depression severity affect CC (sub)volumes.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: One-sample t-test for mean deviation (z-scores); Spearman correlations between HAMD scores and CC (sub)volume z-scores (for whole MDD group, early onset, and mid-to-late onset); Medication was included as a covariate in correlations; Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction for multiple comparisons.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: First-episode MDD patients showed reduced corpus callosum (CC) volume, particularly in mid-to-late onset cases, while early-onset MDD patients exhibited a positive correlation between depression severity and increased CC volume.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Compared to healthy controls, first-episode MDD patients showed significant z-score reductions in the entire corpus callosum (CC) (p=0.04) and CC body (p=0.02, FDR corrected), but depression severity did not influence CC volume in the overall MDD group (p's > 0.05). Mid-to-late onset first-episode MDD patients exhibited significant CC volume z-score decreases in the entire CC (p=0.02) and CC body (p=0.01, FDR corrected). In early-onset first-episode MDD patients, depression severity was positively associated with increased entire CC volume z-scores (r=0.15, p=0.01), including the body (r=0.15, p=0.03, FDR corrected) and splenium (r=0.14, p=0.03, FDR corrected).

caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: No data on depressive episode duration. Relatively small sample size for mid-to-late first-episode MDD patients.; all recruitment sites were in Asia (China).; we could not take into account the duration of the depressive episode; arbitrary choice, and other cut-off scores have been used. Furthermore, the sample size of the mid-to-late-onset first-episode MDD patients was relatively small; lack of this information, other factors such as cognitive information (...), specific depressive characteristics (...), or history or current suicide attempts were not included; we used only three CC subvolumes, but other parcellation atlases of the CC are available.
